pipeline: MNIST uint8 images (torchvision MNIST from the IDX files), cast to float32 with values 0..255, no padding
training set: first K = 4800 images (IDX order); test set: all 10000 images
resize to 14 x 14 with bicubic interpolation (torchvision Resize on the float32 0..255 images, so values may overshoot 0..255)

min-max scaling AFTER the resize: x' = (x - min) / (max - min), with min and max taken over the resized K training images (values in `scaling`); the test images use the same training min and max, so they can fall slightly outside [0, 1]
flattened row-major to resize*resize features, as the network sees them
data.row_order: train_images row i = MNIST training image i (i < K); test rows in IDX order
data.labels: uint8 class 0..9 (ReBoot one-hot pads them to 16 columns; padding columns are always 0)

config_values.lr_note: set in precision_analysis.py's configuration (the --lr argument is not used there)
config_values.lr_schedule: constant for the first 5 epochs (500 steps), then cosine annealing with warm restarts every 50 steps down to 1e-7, stepped once per batch; exact per-step values in per_seed[*].lr_per_step
config_values.optimizer: Nesterov momentum SGD (encrypted variant; the plaintext twin uses the plaintext variant)
config_values.input_resize_note: images resized to resize x resize with bicubic interpolation before flattening
config_values.differs_from_subset_run: the subset run used training_encrypted.py (no resize: 784 inputs; lr from --lr default 5e-4; scheduler stepped once per epoch); the full setting uses precision_analysis.py (14x14 = 196 inputs; scheduler stepped once per batch; trains a plaintext twin alongside)
